subject.title: PR1/5 durable core: residual-gap RFC docs

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this residual durable-core layer as a public architecture direction, or keep TaskFlow and the existing database-first owners canonical and fold any proven gaps into them?
rationale: The documentation is intentionally proposing future core ownership beyond current TaskFlow behavior, and repository policy cannot determine whether that new boundary is desirable without durable-runtime owner intent.

options.title: Fold gaps into existing owners
options.body: Keep TaskFlow and current SQLite-backed owners canonical, converting only concrete missing invariants into focused issues or amendments to their existing docs and contracts.

options.title: Sponsor the public RFC
options.body: Explicitly approve a separate residual durable-core boundary, reconcile it line-by-line with TaskFlow, and treat these pages as the canonical proposal for the implementation stack.

options.title: Keep the RFC internal
options.body: Move the proposal under `docs/internal/` until implementation experiments establish a distinct owner boundary worth publishing.

recommendation.title: Fold gaps into existing owners
recommendation.body: Keep TaskFlow and current SQLite-backed owners canonical, converting only concrete missing invariants into focused issues or amendments to their existing docs and contracts.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and merged the current managed TaskFlow durability boundary that this proposal must complement rather than duplicate.
